## Enzyme Kinetics

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

- The enzyme ($E$) forms a reversible complex with the substrate ($S$).
- The forward reaction results in the formation of a product ($P$) and $E$ returning to its original state.
- Typical enzymatic reactions are instantaneous, and asymptotically approach a certain $P$ concentration.

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

$$E+S \rightleftharpoons ES \rightarrow E+P$$

::: {.fragment}

```{r Enzyme plot}
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 7
tibble(
    time = seq(0, 100, 0.25),
    p    = 10 * time / (10 + time)
) %>%
  ggplot(aes(time, p)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2, color = primary_color) +
  coord_cartesian(expand = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Time", y = "[P]") +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = color_bg),
    panel.grid = element_line(color = color_base),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = color_bg),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = color_bg),
    text = element_text(color = "white"),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "white"),
    axis.line = element_line(color = "white"),
    axis.ticks = element_line(color = "white"),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "white")
  )
```

:::

::: {.fragment}

![](https://cdn.kastatic.org/ka-perseus-images/e72e4f67d724939b0aa31c7fb361e5c8a5976c31.png){.absolute width="450" bottom="200" right="-100"}

:::

## Prion Fibril Kinetics
:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

- Prions form native/misfolded complexes.
- Native prions are integrated into fibrils.
- Fibril nucleation sites remain constant (2 ends of the fibril).
- RT-QuIC speeds up the process but introduces a confounding factor.

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

::: {style="font-size: 0.6em;"}
[Conversion of PrP^C^ to PrP^Fib^]{style="color: #ff4f4f; margin-bottom: 0;"}
$$PrP^C \xrightleftharpoons[k_{-nuc}]{k_{nuc}} PrP^{Nuc} \xrightleftharpoons[k_{-oligo}]{k_{oligo}} PrP^{Oligo} \xrightarrow{k_{fib}} PrP^{Fib}$$

[PrP^Fib^ converting PrP^C^]{style="color: #ff4f4f; margin-bottom: 0;"}
$$PrP^{Fib} + PrP^C \xrightleftharpoons[k_{-nuc}]{k_{nuc}} PrP^{Fib \cdot C} \xrightarrow{k_{fib}} PrP^{Fib + 1}$$
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.absolute bottom="-20" right="-150"}
```{r Prion plot}
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 6
sig_plot <- tibble(
    time = seq(0, 100, 0.25),
    p    = 10 / (1 + exp(0.5 * (50 - time)))
) %>%
  ggplot(aes(time, p)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2, color = primary_color) +
  coord_cartesian(expand = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "Time", y = "[P]") +
  theme(
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = color_bg),
    panel.grid = element_line(color = color_base),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = color_bg),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = color_bg),
    text = element_text(color = "white"),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "white"),
    axis.line = element_line(color = "white"),
    axis.ticks = element_line(color = "white"),
    axis.title = element_text(color = "white")
  )
sig_plot
```
:::

:::

:::

::::

## Why is RT-QuIC sigmoidal?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- A sigmoid would normally suggest some kind of cooperative interaction or feedback loop.
- PrP fibril formation should follow the hyperbolic curve because the fibril formation is linear.
- Why is it sigmoidal?
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.fragment}
::: {style="font-size: 0.6em;"}
[**Fragmentation**]{style="color: #ff4f4f;"}
$$
PrP^{Fib} \xrightarrow{k_{frag}} 2PrP^{Fib}
$$
:::
:::
::: {.fragment}
::: {style="font-size: 0.6em;"}
$$
PrP^{Fib} + PrP^C \xrightleftharpoons[k_{-nuc}]{k_{nuc}} PrP^{Fib \cdot C} \xrightarrow{k_{fib}} PrP^{Fib + 1}\xrightarrow{k_{frag}} 2PrP^{Fib}
$$
:::
:::

::: {.absolute bottom="-20" right="-150"}
```{r}
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 6
sig_plot
```
:::
:::
::::

## How do we get the rate constants?

- Alter [E] and [S] to get the $k_{fib}$ constant.
- Alter RT-QuIC shaking parameters to get $k_{frag}$.
- How will we characterize the reaction given that RT-QuIC frequently shows more structure than a single sigmoid?

::: {.fragment}
::: {.center}

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-width: 6
S1 <- 25
S2 = -7.5
a1 = 1.5
a2 = 0.5
b1 = 10
b2 = 16
df_example <- tibble(time = seq(0, 48, 0.25)) %>%
  mutate(
    growth = S1 / (1 + exp(a1 * (b1 - time))),
    decay = S2 / (1 + exp(a2 * (b2 - time))),
    combined = growth + decay,
    raw = combined + rnorm(length(time), 0, 0.2)
  )

df_example %>%
  ggplot(aes(time, combined)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2, color = "#7c7c7c") +
  geom_point(aes(y = raw), size = 0.5, color = "#adafae") +
  scale_color_manual(values = color_palette) +
  dark_theme +
  theme(
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "inside",
    legend.position.inside = c(0, .95),
    legend.justification = c(0, 1),
    legend.background = element_blank(),
  )

```
:::
:::

# Nonlinear Model

## The Double Sigmoidal Model
:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- We frequently observe a **dampening** effect that pulls the signal back down after the peak.
- Using a nonlinear least-squares regression, we can summarize the data as the **sum of two logistic functions**:
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.fragment}
$$
f(t)=\frac{S_1}{1+e^{a_1(b_1-t)}}+\frac{S_2}{1+e^{a_2(b_2-t)}}
$$
:::
::: {.fragment}
```{r Example Graph}
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-width: 10
example_graph(S1 = 25, S2 = -12.5, a1 = 1.5, a2 = 0.5, b1 = 10, b2 = 16)
```
:::
:::
::::

## Parameter Interpretation

Each sigmoid contributes three parameters — six in total describe a reaction:

| Parameter | Meaning |
|:---:|---|
| S~1~, S~2~ | Asymptotes of 1$^\circ$ / 2$^\circ$ phases |
| a~1~, a~2~ | Steepness of inflection points |
| b~1~, b~2~ | Time to inflection point |

::: {.fragment}
Together, these coefficients form a compact **kinetic fingerprint** for a single RT-QuIC reaction.
:::

## Derived Parameters
::: {style="font-size: 0.6em;"}
| Parameter | Formula | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| $k_{fib}$ | $\dfrac{V_{max}}{[E]}$ | Fibrillation rate constant |
| $k_{frag}$| $\dfrac{1}{b_2-b_1}$ | Fragmentation rate constant |
| $t_{lag}$ | $b_1 - \dfrac{a_1}{2}$ | Alternative lag time estimate |
| $K_M$     | $\frac{k_{fib} + k_{-nuc}}{k_{nuc}}$ | $[S]$ at $\dfrac{V_{max}}{2}$ | 
| $V_{max}$ | $k_{fib}[E]$ | Maximum reaction velocity |
| $v_0$     | $\dfrac{V_{max}[S]}{K_M + [S]}$ | Reaction velocity (Michaelis-Menten equation) |
:::

::: {.fragment}
These give a bridge back to conventional RT-QuIC metrics (like RAF) while retaining the full shape information the double sigmoid captures.
:::

# Current Work: Describing Reaction Kinetics

## Experiment 1: Altering [E] {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="30%"}
- **Question:** Does seed concentration modulate the amplitude, timing, or inflection of either phase?

- **Design:** Serial dilution of a known CWD-positive lymph node sample, run under standard conditions (42°C, 700 rpm, 15 min read cycle, 96 hr).
:::
::: {.column width="70%"}
::: {.fragment}
```{r Load seed data}
#| include: false
seed_files <- list.files("raw/seed_effects", pattern = "*.xlsx", full.names = TRUE)
seed_groups <- c("sample", "well", "dilutions", "rxn")

get_raw <- function(file) {
  file %>%
    get_quic() %>%
    mutate(
      rxn = str_extract(file, "2026\\d{4}_r\\d+_[A-Z]+_\\D+\\."),
      rxn = str_remove(rxn, "\\.")
    )
}

seed_raw <- seed_files %>%
  map_dfr(get_raw) %>%
  clean_names(replace = c("Sample IDs" = "sample")) %>%
  filter(time > 0) %>%
  normalize("time", "rfu", 8, seed_groups, 3) %>%
  mutate(
    across(c(sample, well, rxn), as.factor),
    dilutions = -log10(as.integer(dilutions))
  ) %>%
  na.omit()

seed_df <- seed_raw %>%
  nest(.by = all_of(seed_groups)) %>%
  left_join(
    calculate_metrics(
      seed_raw, seed_groups, threshold = 3,
      time_col = "time", ttt_values = "norm", auc_values = "norm",
      norm_col = "norm", deriv_col = "deriv"
    ),
    by = seed_groups
  ) %>%
  filter(MPR > 3) %>%
  estimate_params() %>%
  na.omit()

seed_mod <- seed_df %>%
  mutate(model = pmap(., fit_model, single_only = FALSE, weighted = TRUE)) %>%
  filter(map_lgl(model, ~ inherits(.x, "nls"))) %>%
  mutate(coefficients = map(model, coef)) %>%
  unnest_wider(coefficients)
```

```{r Seed vs Parameters}
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 12
seed_mod %>%
  pivot_longer(c(S1, a1, b1, S2, a2, b2), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "value") %>%
  filter(
    value >= (quantile(value, 0.25) - 1.5 * IQR(value)) &
      value <= (quantile(value, 0.75) + 1.5 * IQR(value)),
    .by = parameter
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    hline = ifelse(parameter == "S2", 0, NA),
    parameter = factor(
      parameter,
      levels = c("S1", "a1", "b1", "S2", "a2", "b2"),
      labels = c(TeX("$S_1$"), TeX("$a_1$"), TeX("$b_1$"), TeX("$S_2$"), TeX("$a_2$"), TeX("$b_2$"))
    )
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(dilutions, value, color = dilutions)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.05)) +
  geom_rug(sides = "l") +
  stat_smooth(method = "loess") +
  geom_line(aes(dilutions, hline), linetype = "dashed", color = "white", linewidth = 1, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  stat_cor(aes(label = paste(after_stat(rr.label), after_stat(p.label), sep = "~`,`~")), geom = "label", size = 4, fill = "black", color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(vars(parameter), scales = "free_y", labeller = label_parsed) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "darkcyan", high = "darkorange") +
  labs(x = TeX(r'(Log$_{10}$ Seed Dilution Factor)'), y = "Coefficient Value") +
  dark_theme +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(color="white", size = 24)
  )
```

:::
:::
::::


## Experiment 2: [S] {.smaller}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="30%"}
- **Question:** Does substrate concentration modulate either phase, and does it behave like classical enzyme kinetics?

- **Design:** Fixed seed dilution ($10^{-3}$), substrate concentration varied from 0.01 to 0.4 µg/µL, standard reaction conditions.
:::

::: {.column width="70%"}
::: {.fragment}
```{r Load substrate data}
#| include: false
sub_files <- list.files("raw/substrate_effects", pattern = "*.xlsx", full.names = TRUE)
sub_groups <- c("sample", "well", "dilutions", "rxn")

sub_raw <- sub_files %>%
  map_dfr(get_raw) %>%
  clean_names(replace = c("Sample IDs" = "sample")) %>%
  filter(time > 0) %>%
  normalize("time", "rfu", 8, sub_groups, 3) %>%
  mutate(
    across(c(sample, well, rxn), as.factor),
    dilutions = as.integer(dilutions) / 1000
  ) %>%
  na.omit()

sub_df <- sub_raw %>%
  nest(.by = all_of(sub_groups)) %>%
  estimate_params() %>%
  na.omit()

sub_mod <- sub_df %>%
  mutate(model = pmap(., fit_model, single_only = FALSE, weighted = TRUE)) %>%
  filter(map_lgl(model, ~ inherits(.x, "nls"))) %>%
  mutate(coefficients = map(model, coef)) %>%
  unnest_wider(coefficients) %>%
  mutate(v = 1 / b1)
```


```{r Substrate vs Parameters}
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-width: 12
sub_mod %>%
  pivot_longer(c(S1, a1, b1, S2, a2, b2), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "value") %>%
  filter(
    value >= (quantile(value, 0.25) - 1.5 * IQR(value)) &
      value <= (quantile(value, 0.75) + 1.5 * IQR(value)),
    .by = parameter
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    hline = ifelse(parameter == "S2", 0, NA),
    parameter = factor(
      parameter,
      levels = c("S1", "a1", "b1", "S2", "a2", "b2"),
      labels = c(TeX("$S_1$"), TeX("$a_1$"), TeX("$b_1$"), TeX("$S_2$"), TeX("$a_2$"), TeX("$b_2$"))
    )
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(dilutions, value, color = dilutions)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.01)) +
  geom_rug(sides = "l") +
  stat_smooth(method = "loess") +
  geom_line(aes(dilutions, hline), linetype = "dashed", color = "white", linewidth = 1, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  stat_cor(aes(label = paste(after_stat(rr.label), after_stat(p.label), sep = "~`,`~")), geom = "label", size = 4, fill = "black", color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(vars(parameter), scales = "free_y", labeller = label_parsed) +
  scale_color_gradient(low = "darkcyan", high = "darkorange") +
  labs(x = "[Substrate] (mg/mL)", y = "Coefficient Value") +
  dark_theme +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

:::

::::

## Determining $V_{max}$ and $K_{fib}$

::: {style="font-size: 0.6em;"}
Treating $1/b_1$ as a reaction velocity and fitting $v = \dfrac{V_{max}[S]}{K_{fib} + [S]}$ up to the peak:
:::

```{r Vmax fit}
sub_summary <- sub_mod %>%
  summarize(across(c(v), mean), .by = c(sample, dilutions))

vmax <- max(sub_summary$v)
vmax_substrate <- sub_summary[which.max(sub_summary$v), ]$dilutions
Km <- sub_summary[which.max(sub_summary$v <= vmax / 2), ]$dilutions

sub_to_max <- sub_mod %>% filter(dilutions <= vmax_substrate)

nls_mod <- nls(
  v ~ (Vmax * dilutions) / (Km + dilutions),
  data = sub_to_max,
  start = list(Vmax = vmax, Km = Km),
  algorithm = "port"
)

mic_men <- tibble(
  dilutions = seq(-0.1, 0.5, by = 0.01),
  v = (coef(nls_mod)[1] * dilutions) / (coef(nls_mod)[2] + dilutions),
  d_inv = 1 / dilutions,
  v_inv = 1 / v
) %>%
  filter(dilutions != 0)
```

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}

```{r}
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 9
sub_mod %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = dilutions, y = v)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.01, seed = 157093759), color = "darkorange") +
  geom_line(data = mic_men, aes(x = dilutions, y = v), color = "darkorange", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 0.4, by = 0.05), limits = c(0, 0.4)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(
    title = "Saturation Plot",
    x = "[Substrate] (mg/mL)", 
    y = TeX("V ($h^{-1}$)")
  ) +
  dark_theme
```
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| fig-height: 5
#| fig-width: 9
sub_mod %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = 1/dilutions, y = 1/v)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "white", linewidth = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, color = "white", linewidth = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = 0.01, seed = 157093759), color = "darkorange") +
  geom_line(data = mic_men, aes(x = d_inv, y = v_inv), color = "darkorange", linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-100, 100, by = 25), limits = c(-20, NA)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-10, NA)) +
  coord_cartesian(expand = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Lineweaver-Burk Plot",
    x = TeX("\\[S]$^{-1}$ (mL/mg)"), 
    y = TeX("V$^{-1}$ (h)")
  ) +
  dark_theme
```
:::

::: {style="font-size: 0.6em;"}
Theoretical $V_{max} = `r round(coef(nls_mod)[1], 2)`\ h^{-1}$, theoretical $K_m = `r round(coef(nls_mod)[2], 2)`\ mg/mL$.
:::

## Next Steps

- **Fragmentation dynamics**: does shaking speed / temperature shift the secondary phase, implicating mechanical fragmentation?
- **Orthogonal measurements**: do absorbance (A600), SyproOrange, and Bradford assays confirm the secondary phase as a real change in fibril/soluble protein state, or is it ThT-specific?
- **Generalizability**: does the biphasic profile, and its secondary-phase parameters, hold across prion strains and substrate species, and can this model be used to predict certain characteristics of the initial prion seed?
